Run a template

A template is a ready-made query written against named columns rather than one particular file. You tell it which of your columns to use, and it writes the SQL with your column names in it. This example runs one on the sample shipments, so you can follow along without a file of your own.

  1. In the header, select Templates. You can also press Ctrl+K (⌘+K on a Mac) and choose Browse templates.
  2. Choose On-time delivery by carrier.
  3. If the shipments table isn't loaded yet, select Load sample data in the Shipments box. The form fills in the table and its columns.
  4. Check the column each field uses. To count deliveries up to a day late as on time, set Days of grace to 1.
  5. Select Run.

The dialog closes, the template's SQL goes into the editor and runs, and the result opens as a chart. Here it's a bar chart of on_time_pct by carrier. Select Table to see the rows. The first line of the query is a comment with the template's title, such as -- On-time delivery by carrier. The query is now yours, so you can change it and run it again like any other. To read the result, see Explore results.

The gallery lists the templates in alphabetical order. Below they're grouped by the kind of data they read. Each one runs out of the box on one of the samples, named under its title.

How column matching works

When you open a template, it makes a first guess at every choice in the form.

  • For each table the template needs, it picks the sample table if that's loaded. Otherwise it picks the table whose columns match the most fields.
  • A field matches a column with the same name as the field, its label or one of a few common alternatives, ignoring case, spaces, underscores and hyphens. So Machine ID, machine_id and machine-id all match the Machine field.
  • The column also has to be the right type, and each column is used for one field at most.

Because a loaded sample table wins, choose your own table under Table if you've loaded both. Changing the table matches its columns again. You can then change any field by hand. Each list shows your columns with their types.

Fields have one of four types:

  • Text accepts a text column, and a number column too, since labels such as machine numbers are often stored as numbers.
  • Number accepts an integer or decimal column.
  • Date or time accepts a DATE or TIMESTAMP column. The form calls this type "temporal". A date stored as text doesn't count. Files with dates written as 2026-09-21 or 2026-09-21 14:00 are usually read as dates.
  • Any accepts every column.

A field marked (optional) can stay at None. While something stops the template from running, Run is unavailable and the form says why next to it, for example "Choose a column for Machine." or "Started at needs a temporal column; started_at is VARCHAR."

Production templates

These read machine logs, breakdown logs, output reports and inspections, as an MES or a shop-floor system exports them.

OEE by machine

Each machine's overall equipment effectiveness over its planned minutes, split into availability, performance and quality, best machine first. It expects one row per machine per minute, because it counts rows as minutes. Runs on machine_telemetry. The result has planned_min, run_min, availability_pct, performance_pct, quality_pct and oee_pct.

FieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
MachineTextmachine_id, machine, asset, equipment, station
Minute (optional)Date or timeminute_at, timestamp, time, date
PlannedAny, true or false valuesplanned, scheduled, is_planned
RunningAny, true or false valuesrunning, is_running, producing, active
Ideal cycle (s)Numberideal_cycle_s, ideal_cycle, cycle_time, ct
Total countNumbertotal_count, total, parts, units, output
Good countNumbergood_count, good, good_parts, ok_count

Downtime Pareto

Minutes of downtime and the number of stops for each reason, largest first, with each reason's share and the running share of all downtime. It opens as a Pareto chart. Runs on breakdowns. The result has downtime_min, stops, machines, share_pct and cumulative_pct.

FieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
ReasonTextreason, cause, stop_reason, fault, code
Started atDate or timestarted_at, start, start_time, from
Ended atDate or timeended_at, end, end_time, finished_at, to
Machine (optional)Textmachine, machine_id, asset, equipment

MTTR and MTBF per machine

Mean time to repair and mean time between failures for each machine, worst MTBF first. MTBF is the time from one breakdown's end to the next one's start on the same machine, so a machine with a single breakdown has no MTBF. Runs on breakdowns. The result has failures, downtime_h, mttr_min and mtbf_h.

FieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
MachineTextmachine, machine_id, asset, equipment, station
Started atDate or timestarted_at, start, start_time, began_at
Ended atDate or timeended_at, end, end_time, stopped_at

Output by production day and shift

Units and events per production day and shift, and per machine if you map one. The production day starts with the first shift, so a night shift that runs past midnight counts towards the day it started. Set Shift starts (default 06:00, 14:00, 22:00) and Shift names (default A, B, C) to match your plant. Runs on shift_output.

FieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
Event atDate or timeevent_at, timestamp, time, reported_at
UnitsNumberunits, quantity, qty, count, output
Machine (optional)Textmachine, machine_id, asset, station, line

Reject rate by machine

Parts inspected and rejected on each machine, and the share rejected, worst machine first. To leave out machines with few inspections, raise Minimum inspected from 0. Runs on quality_checks. The result has inspected, rejected and reject_rate_pct.

FieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
MachineTextmachine_id, machine, asset, station
Checked at (optional)Date or timechecked_at, timestamp, date, inspected_at
InspectedNumberinspected, quantity, qty, parts, checked
RejectedNumberrejected, rejects, defects, scrap, ng

Logistics templates

These read one row per shipment, as a transport management system exports it. All three run on shipments. A shipment with no delivery date counts as still in transit.

On-time delivery by carrier

The share of each carrier's delivered shipments that arrived by the promised date, worst carrier first. Dates are compared as calendar days. Shipments in transit are counted but left out of the rate, as they may still arrive on time. Days of grace counts deliveries up to that many days late as on time. The result has delivered, on_time, late, in_transit, on_time_pct and avg_days_late.

FieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
CarrierTextcarrier, carrier_name, scac, haulier, courier
Promised deliveryDate or timepromised_date, due_date, expected_delivery, eta
DeliveredDate or timedelivered_date, delivered_at, delivery_date, pod_date

Delivery lead time by lane

The median and 90th percentile of calendar days from shipping to delivery on each lane, slowest lane first, with the number delivered and still in transit. A lane is the origin and destination together, such as Pune → Delhi. The 90th percentile is the time within which 9 in 10 shipments arrive. The result has delivered, in_transit, median_days and p90_days.

FieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
OriginTextorigin, from, ship_from, origin_city
DestinationTextdestination, to, dest, ship_to
ShippedDate or timeship_date, shipped_at, dispatch_date, pickup_date
DeliveredDate or timedelivered_date, delivered_at, delivery_date, pod_date

Cost per kg by lane and carrier

Freight cost per kilogram for each carrier on each lane, cheapest carrier first within a lane, with the weight moved and what it cost. It divides total cost by total weight, so heavy shipments count for more than light ones. The result has shipments, weight_kg, cost and cost_per_kg.

FieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
OriginTextorigin, from, ship_from, origin_city
DestinationTextdestination, to, dest, ship_to
CarrierTextcarrier, carrier_name, scac, haulier, courier
Weight (kg)Numberweight_kg, weight, kg, gross_weight, chargeable_weight
Freight costNumberfreight_cost, cost, freight, total_cost, amount

Reconciliation and data-quality templates

These compare two files, or check one file before it's loaded into another system.

Two-file reconciliation

Every key where two systems, such as an ERP and an MES, disagree. A key is listed when it's missing on one side or has a different quantity, largest variance first. Each side's quantities are added up per key first, and keys are compared as text, so 1001 matches '1001'. The status column says Only in first, Only in second or Quantities differ. Tolerance leaves out keys found on both sides whose quantities differ by no more than that amount. Runs on erp_orders and mes_orders, whose columns have different names, as they often do in real exports.

Table and fieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
First system (e.g. ERP), KeyTextkey, order_id, work_order, order_number
First system (e.g. ERP), QuantityNumberquantity, qty, reported_qty, confirmed_qty
Second system (e.g. MES), KeyTextkey, order_id, work_order, order_number
Second system (e.g. MES), QuantityNumberquantity, qty, good_qty, produced_qty

Data-quality checks for an import file

Duplicate keys, missing mandatory fields and references to codes that don't exist, one row per issue, so you can fix a file before it's migrated. The issue column says Duplicate key, Missing followed by the column's name, or Broken reference, and row_number counts from 1 in file order. Map up to three mandatory fields. To check references, map Reference to the column that holds a code and choose the table that lists the valid codes. The form asks for a reference table even if you leave Reference at None. Runs on item_import and plants.

Table and fieldTypeMatches columns named, for example
Import file, KeyAnykey, item_code, code, id, sku
Import file, Mandatory field 1 (optional)Anydescription, name, item_description
Import file, Mandatory field 2 (optional)Anyuom, unit, unit_of_measure, base_unit
Import file, Mandatory field 3 (optional)AnyNo other names. Choose it yourself.
Import file, Reference (optional)Anyreference, plant_code, plant, site, warehouse
Reference table, Reference keyAnyplant_code, plant, code, id

To change a template's output, such as adding a filter by date, run it and then edit its query in the editor. Write queries covers the editor.
